title: Bull Durham
about: A veteran catcher is brought in to train a wild young pitcher, and they both catch the eye of the same woman.

    StartersHit Bull Win Steak ballpark franksGrilled franks in soft buns with yellow mustard and pickle relishHow to make it8 hot dog franks8 hot dog buns3 tbsp yellow mustard4 tbsp pickle relishGrill the franks until they split and blister.Tuck each into a soft bun with a stripe of mustard and a spoon of relish.Wrap tightly in paper so the bun steams.Carolina hushpuppiesFried cornmeal and onion fritters, crisp outside, soft insideHow to make it1 cup fine cornmeal1/2 cup self-raising flour1 tbsp caster sugar1 onion, grated1 egg180ml buttermilk1 L vegetable oil, for fryingbutter or hot sauce, to serveWhisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar and onion with the egg and buttermilk.Heat the oil to about 5cm deep.Drop teaspoons into the hot oil and fry until golden.Drain and serve with butter or hot sauce.Dugout hot honey roasted peanutsCrash and Nuke killing time in the dugoutHow to make itAs written, serves 4Raw peanuts roasted with butter, honey, brown sugar and cayenne until glossy and crunchy, finished with flaky salt and served warm in paper bags.Heat the oven to 170°C.Melt 30g butter with 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp brown sugar, half a tsp cayenne and 1 tsp salt.Toss with 400g raw unsalted peanuts until coated.Spread on a lined tray and roast 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until deep golden.Sprinkle with flaky salt and leave to cool on the tray for 10 minutes so they crisp.Break up any clumps and scoop into paper bags.Fried okra with comeback sauceBreathe through your eyelids, like the lava lizards.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsCarolina pulled porkPork shoulder roasted until it pulls apart, tangy cider vinegar sauceHow to make it2kg pork shoulder1 tbsp salt250ml apple cider vinegar3 tbsp brown sugar1 tsp chilli flakes8 burger buns1/2 small cabbageRub the pork with salt and roast covered at 150°C until it pulls apart.Simmer the vinegar with the brown sugar and chilli flakes.Shred the pork and toss through the sauce. Shred the cabbage for a slaw and dress it with a splash of the sauce.Pile the pork into buns with the slaw.Annie's buttermilk fried chickenAnnie Savoy's house, where the season's lessons happenHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken drumsticks soaked overnight in spiced buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour and fried until crackling, with creamy mash and peppery gravy.Soak 8 drumsticks overnight in 500ml buttermilk with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp hot sauce.Mix 250g plain flour with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp pepper and 1 tsp salt.Dredge the chicken, pressing to coat.Fry in oil at 160°C for 12 to 14 minutes until cooked through to 75°C inside.Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and milk.For gravy, whisk 2 tbsp of the frying flour into 2 tbsp butter, then 400ml chicken stock and plenty of pepper.SweetsCarolina banana puddingVanilla custard layered with bananas and sweet biscuitsHow to make it4 egg yolks120g caster sugar50g cornflour750ml milk20g butter2 tsp vanilla extract250g vanilla wafer biscuits4 bananas300ml thickened cream1 tbsp icing sugarWhisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour in a saucepan, then whisk in the milk.Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick.Off the heat, stir in the butter and vanilla. Cover the surface and cool.Layer the wafers, sliced bananas and custard in a dish, repeating twice.Whip the cream with icing sugar and spread on top.Chill, ideally overnight.DrinksNuke LaLoosh bourbon sweet teaSweet black tea with bourbon, lemon and mint over iceHow to make it4 black tea bags1 L water, just boiled80g brown sugar180ml bourbon2 lemons4 sprigs of mint2 cups iceSteep the tea bags in the just boiled water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in the sugar until dissolved.Cool, then chill.Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, add bourbon and tea to each and squeeze in a lemon wedge.Slap a mint sprig between your hands and drop it in.
